CacheControlNoStore.description: Prevents storage of error responses by clients and intermediaries.

AssignRequestID.description: Assign-Request-ID on every response; X-Request-ID is its correlation alias.

ContentTypeOptions.description: Prevents user agents from MIME-sniffing the response.

AssignAPIVersion.description: Assign-API-Version diagnostic, never authorization or an old-contract selector.

WWWAuthenticate.description: Applicable bearer challenge on product authentication failures.

AssignLimit.description: Assign application limit metadata version 1, independent of draft IETF RateLimit fields. The closed kind/scope/policy/unit labels identify the applicable existing budget, never a bucket, credential, actor identifier or private queue depth. The search class is query cost (one admitted query unit), not paid entitlement. cost is the units required by this request; limit/remaining are window units when known; reset is Unix seconds. Concurrent and entitlement outcomes omit unknown counters. A reset or Retry-After is earliest retry guidance, not guaranteed admission. Honor Retry-After within the caller deadline, use bounded backoff with jitter and do not loop automatically on quota/entitlement failures.

AssignDeadlineMs.description: Remaining request time budget at admission in milliseconds, capped by any earlier deadline already applied to the request. The value is diagnostic; client-supplied values do not extend work. Cancellation is cooperative and bounds work that observes it. A timeout or disconnect does not prove that a committed mutation rolled back; recover using the operation's retained idempotency key/receipt before issuing another mutation. Committed responses are preserved.

RetryAfter.description: Retry-After delay-seconds or HTTP-date; honor within the caller deadline.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed or fails validation.

Unauthorized.description: Authentication is missing, invalid, expired, or revoked.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist or is not visible to this principal.

ProductProblem.description: An HTTP admission, validation, domain or availability failure. The status and code select a catalog entry. Errors use no-store; 401 includes WWW-Authenticate, 405 includes Allow, and 429/503 include Retry-After. Stream errors use this response only before the stream is committed.

Conflict.description: The mutation conflicts with current resource state or idempotency history.

TooManyRequests.description: The caller has exceeded an applicable abuse-control limit.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the client may retry.

InternalServerError.description: The server could not complete the request.

MaintenanceUnavailable.description:
Scheduled maintenance temporarily prevents this operation. The standard
Problem Details response has reason `maintenance_offline` when the service is
unavailable. Mutating operations may instead return
`maintenance_read_only` while reads remain available. Clients must
treat both reasons as retryable availability states, not authorization
failures, and honor `Retry-After` when present.

Retry-After.description: Delay in seconds before retrying, when an expected maintenance end is known.
